vulnerabilities.description: Missing authentication check on booking creation endpoint. Any unauthenticated user can create bookings for any property. Endpoint should verify user identity before processing bookings.

Missing input validation on propertyId parameter in getProperty(). While Supabase RLS provides protection, explicit validation at application layer is missing. Should validate UUID format and existence.
Untrusted image URLs from database not validated. Property images array could contain malicious URLs. Should validate against whitelist of trusted image domains.
No rate limiting on POST /api/bookings endpoint. Attackers can spam booking creation requests for denial of service. Should implement rate limiting per IP/user.
Detailed validation error disclosure to client. Returns parsed.error.flatten() which exposes schema structure. Should return generic error messages to clients.
No CORS headers configured. Missing explicit CORS policy configuration. Should define allowed origins.
No CSRF token on booking form submission. POST request lacks CSRF protection. Should implement CSRF tokens using Next.js middleware.
Session context data stored in plaintext JSON file. If sensitive data is stored in context, it's exposed. Should encrypt sensitive session data.

Supabase anon key in public environment variables (by design). While NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix indicates this is intentional, security depends entirely on Row-Level Security (RLS) configuration in Supabase, which cannot be verified from codebase.
No dependency scanning for known vulnerabilities. Should run 'npm audit' and pin critical dependencies to known-good versions.

recommendations: URGENT: Implement authentication middleware for /api/bookings endpoint. Use NextAuth.js or similar to verify user identity before creating bookings.
Add input validation: Validate property IDs are valid UUIDs and exist before querying. Validate all user inputs at API boundaries.
Implement rate limiting on all API endpoints using a library like 'next-rate-limit' or middleware approach.
Add CSRF protection: Use Next.js CSRF middleware and include tokens in form submissions.
Validate image URLs: Implement domain whitelist for property images from Supabase.
Remove detailed validation errors from API responses. Return generic error messages to clients, log details server-side only.
Verify Supabase Row-Level Security (RLS) is properly configured to prevent unauthorized data access.
Configure explicit CORS headers in Next.js middleware specifying allowed origins.
Run 'npm audit' and update vulnerable dependencies. Add 'npm audit' to CI/CD pipeline.
Encrypt sensitive session data before storing to disk.
Add Content Security Policy (CSP) headers to prevent XSS attacks.

mainConcerns: Missing rate limiting and CSRF protection
